title: office-art-and-plants-guidelines-2024
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Title: Office Art & Plant Guidelines

Summary:
This page documents lightweight guidelines for installing office art, plants, and temporary desk decorations at Redwood Inference offices. It is intended to balance aesthetic expression with safety, accessibility, and shared workspace norms. These notes are informal and maintained by People Ops.

Scope:
- Applies to common areas (kitchen, lounges, corridors) and individual desks in open offices.
- Does not replace formal safety or building management policies for structural changes or electrical work.

Guiding Principles:
1. Safety first: no obstructing egress, fire alarms, or emergency equipment. Avoid tripping hazards.
2. Respect shared spaces: avoid strong scents, noisy installations, or items that monopolize common areas.
3. Accessibility: ensure signage/art is hung at a height that does not impede mobility or visibility.
4. Temporary & reversible: most installations should be removable without tools or wall damage.

Approval & Ownership:
- Small desk plants and framed prints: no formal approval required.
- Larger items (floor-standing planters, freestanding sculptures, wall-hung installations > 30" in any dimension): submit a short request to people-ops@redwood.com with location, dimensions, weight, and installation method.
- People Ops is the owner for approvals and coordination with building management.

Installation Guidelines:
- Mounting: prefer adhesive strips rated for drywall where appropriate; for heavier fixtures require building-approved anchors and sign-off.
- Electrical: any installation requiring power must be scheduled with facilities and IT; do not run extension cords across walkways.
- Plants: prefer low-allergen, low-light tolerant species for shared spaces (e.g., snake plant, pothos). Avoid high-fragrance plants in kitchens and meeting rooms.
- ID tags: label any communal plant with owner name and watering cadence if not centrally maintained.

Maintenance & Removal:
- Owners are responsible for upkeep. Facilities may remove items that create hazards or persistent nuisances after one week's notice.
- For space reconfigurations, owners will be asked to relocate or remove personal/communal items within two weeks.

Temporary Exhibitions & Events:
- If a team wants to host a temporary exhibit (art show, maker fair, holiday display), submit a proposal at least 10 business days prior including insurance/waiver details if items are valuable.

Quick Checklist (for submitters):
- [ ] Location & footprint
- [ ] Estimated weight
- [ ] Mounting method
- [ ] Owner & contact
- [ ] Maintenance plan
- [ ] Needed approvals (building/facilities)

Contacts & Related Pages:
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com
- Facilities manager: facilities@redwood.com
- Related Confluence: [Company Handbook - Office Policies](/confluence/company-handbook/office-policies)
- Related Confluence: [Space Allocation Guide](/confluence/people-ops/space-allocation)

Notes:
- This guidance is intentionally lightweight to encourage a pleasant workplace while keeping operations simple. For complex installations or anything involving building infrastructure, coordinate with Facilities and People Ops.
